title: Lesson 18 - Turning Discovery into a Solution: Prioritized Use-Case Backlog
description: Conduct discovery workshops, analyze business requirements, define solutions, and prioritize use cases.

questions.question: Twelve use cases are all marked Must in the MoSCoW rankings. What does that tell you?
options: The list is complete and safe to sign into the SOW
The Must threshold has become meaningless and you need a forcing constraint to re-rank
MoSCoW was applied correctly and the sponsor can proceed
You should switch the ranking to alphabetical order to settle ties
questions.explanation: When every item is a Must the tier no longer discriminates, so a real constraint such as budget, date, or capacity is what re-ranks the list; signing an undifferentiated Must list into the SOW turns every wish into a contractual obligation.

questions.question: Data quality in the target objects is poor and unverified, and the client wants the highest-value use case shipped first. What do you sequence first?
options: The highest-value use case regardless of the state of the data
Whichever use case the loudest executive sponsors
A data-remediation foundation slice, because a use case is only as good as the data underneath it
Every use case at once to save elapsed time
questions.explanation: Value cannot be realized on unreliable data, so a data-remediation foundation slice comes first even though it is less visible; sequencing the high-value use case onto bad data teaches the organization to distrust the platform.

questions.question: A client wants a thin end-to-end pilot before committing budget to the full build. What is the best artifact to sequence that pilot?
options: A full technical design document covering every object and integration
A change order against the existing statement of work
A steering committee charter defining decision rights
A walking skeleton, one vertical slice through the real stack, that proves the integration and adoption risk
questions.explanation: A walking skeleton runs one true path from user action through automation and integration to output, which exposes integration and adoption risk while it is still cheap; a horizontal layer would prove each layer in isolation and defer the mismatch.
